fullPassage: The million-dollar question where courage is concerned is whether or not courage can be learned. If fear and courage are to be found at least in part in the hard-wiring of our brains, then it certainly makes sense to assume that there is a genetic component to bravery. If bravery is simply a personality trait, then there isn't much point in trying to learn how to do it better. Fortunately, the research suggests there is hope for people who want to boost their courage quotient. Studies show that people — as many as 82 percent of those studied — overwhelmingly opt to try courage-enhancing strategies to help them face difficult circumstances. Actors who are nervous before opening night spend time on the stage, familiarizing themselves with the auditorium; boxers strut and look angry to overcome the butterflies in their stomachs; people pray or knock on wood or wear favorite pieces of clothing, all because they think this will help to give them a more favorable outcome and allow them to face an uncertain, even risky future.

det.analysis:
✅ ① 용기 향상 전략이 존재하고 82%가 이를 시도한다는 본문 핵심과 일치 ←정답
❌ ② 유전자의 결정적 영향이 아니라 학습 가능성이 주제
❌ ③ 두려움 완전 제거는 본문에서 다루지 않음
❌ ④ 기도는 예시 중 하나일 뿐 종교적 기능이 주제가 아님
det.tip: 'courage-enhancing strategies'와 '82 percent'가 주제의 핵심 키워드입니다.

위험한 미래에 대비하는 종교적 신앙의 심리적 기능

questions.passage: The million-dollar question where courage is concerned is whether or not courage can be learned. If fear and courage are to be found at least in part in the hard-wiring of our brains, then it certainly makes sense to assume that there is a genetic component to bravery. If bravery is simply a personality trait, then there isn't much point in trying to learn how to do it better. Fortunately, the research suggests there is hope for people who want to boost their courage quotient. Studies show that people — as many as 82 percent of those studied — overwhelmingly opt to try courage-enhancing strategies to help them face difficult circumstances. Actors who are nervous before opening night spend time on the stage, familiarizing themselves with the auditorium; boxers strut and look angry to overcome <u>the butterflies in their stomachs</u>; people pray or knock on wood or wear favorite pieces of clothing, all because they think this will help to give them a more favorable outcome and allow them to face an uncertain, even risky future.
questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>the butterflies in their stomachs</u>이(가) 다음 글에서 의미하는 바로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 'butterflies in one's stomach'이라는 관용표현의 문맥적 의미를 파악한다.
det.analysis:
❌ ① 위협 전략이 아니라 극복 대상에 해당
❌ ② 피로감이 아니라 심리적 긴장감을 나타내는 관용구
✅ ③ 'butterflies in one's stomach'은 긴장감/불안감을 뜻하는 관용표현으로, 권투선수가 이를 극복하려 한다는 맥락과 일치 ←정답
❌ ④ 체계적 훈련은 본문에서 언급되지 않는 개념
det.tip: 권투선수가 으스대고 화난 표정을 짓는 이유와 연결 지어 생각하세요.

ch: 권투 경기에서 상대를 위협하기 위한 전략적 행동
무대 위에서 경험하는 신체적 피로감과 탈진 상태

questions.stem: 밑줄 친 <u>them</u>이(가) 가리키는 대상으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 'help them face difficult circumstances'에서 them이 누구인지 앞 문맥에서 찾는다.
det.analysis:
✅ ① 'help them face difficult circumstances'에서 them은 바로 앞의 'people'(용기 강화 전략을 시도하는 사람들)을 가리킴 ←정답
❌ ② 배우는 이후 예시에서 등장하며 them의 직접 선행사가 아님

det.tip: 'Studies show that people ... overwhelmingly opt to try'에서 주어를 확인하세요.
